profiles.summary: The Salvador hardfork at mainnet block 98,688,600 (about 2026-12-08) puts code at five externally owned accounts through BlockAlloc during block finalisation. The step runs outside any transaction, and storage and balances are left as they are. This is the first time the mechanism is used on accounts that are not system or genesis contracts. codeReadCache in parallel_statedb.go is the same in v2.11.2, v2.12.0-beta and develop.

deltas.delta: changeContractCodeIfNeeded calls state.SetCode for every address in BlockAlloc[block] and sets the balance only when it is zero (consensus/bor/bor.go lines 1381-1398). It is called during finalisation at line 1289 and in the two assemble paths at lines 1441 and 1501. The mainnet BlockAlloc at 98,688,600 lists 0xe4C4C39C..., 0x53925878..., 0xc91ee057..., 0x3f701922... (Polymarket, recovery 0x4dF68703...) and 0x5227f603... (Binance, recovery 0xd9fD3910...).

The PR states that the hardfork adds no new consensus rule, that sweep() can be called by anyone and sends the address's whole native balance to RECOVERY, and that plain POL transfers to these addresses revert afterwards. Amoy activates at 54,310,900 (2026-12-01) and mainnet at 98,688,600 (2026-12-08). It is on develop and was reverted on the v2.12.0-beta branch.

findings.title: Polygon's Salvador hardfork rewrites the code of five accounts at block 98,688,600 through BlockAlloc, a mechanism that can give any address new code outside a transaction
findings.difference: Bor applies a per-block code table (BlockAlloc) during block finalisation. For every listed address it calls SetCode and keeps the storage, and it sets the balance only when the balance is zero. Ethereum has no rule that replaces an account's code. Polygon has used the table on 0x1001, 0x1010 and WMATIC before. Salvador, scheduled for 2026-12-08, is the first use on accounts that are not system or genesis contracts.
findings.mechanism: At block 98,688,600 the five Polymarket and Binance accounts get a 344 byte sweeper. A call with value reverts, and sweep() sends the native balance to a fixed recovery Safe. For the PoolManager, an address that changes code under BlockAlloc behaves differently through each of the calls it makes. A native take to that address (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52) reverts afterwards. A token take or sync on it (src/types/Currency.sol:53-80 and 90-95) calls code the pool creator never saw. A hook at that address (Hooks.sol permission bits at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:27) answers with other code. The PoolManager's own code could be replaced the same way, and noDelegateCall (src/NoDelegateCall.sol:19-25) does not detect that. The five Salvador targets hold no ERC-6909 claims at the PoolManager in currency 0 (native), USDC, USDC.e, WPOL, USDT or WETH, and no PositionManager position (eth_call at block 97,906,958), so the scheduled rewrite touches no PoolManager funds.
findings.impact: None for the Salvador entries as scheduled. In general, a BlockAlloc entry for a pooled token, a hook or the PoolManager would decide every pool that uses that address. On 2026-11-24 the PoolManager holds 3,211,373 POL and 7,903 WPOL.
findings.preconditions: A bor release with a BlockAlloc entry, adopted by the validator set through Polygon governance (a PIP and a coordinated release). No ordinary account can add an entry.
findings.mitigations: At each bor release, read params/config.go BlockAlloc for the PoolManager, PositionManager and pooled currencies and hooks. After block 98,688,600, compare the code at the five addresses with the table.

cleared.check: Do bor v2.11.2 and the unreleased develop branch change the interpreter, the integer library or state handling compared with the builds already tested?
cleared.result: 17 core/vm and core/state files are byte-identical between v2.11.1 and v2.11.2. develop is identical to v2.12.0-beta in 14 core/vm files and in parallel_statedb.go, blockchain.go and worker.go. Every tag and branch pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. The opcode handlers call SDiv, SMod, Exp, AddMod and MulMod with the result aliasing the last operand (instructions.go lines 60, 74, 81, 196 and 202). The library writes the result only after the computation, so the aliasing is harmless. The only correctness fix in a recent release, v1.3.1's DivMod aliasing fix, is a function the interpreter does not call.

cleared.check: Lead L-750: the cache that --precompile-cache adds in bor v2.12.0-beta. What is its key, and can a STATICCALL from sync(X) get a cached result for a different input or a different precompile?
cleared.result: The flag adds the extended keccak store, keyed by string(data) (shared_cache.go lines 160-245), and gives the builder and the serial importer the ecrecover cache. The ecrecover cache serves only address 0x01 with input of at most 128 bytes. Its key is the input right-padded to 128 bytes, which is the padding ecrecover applies anyway. It is skipped when the precompile set is overridden. Gas is charged from RequiredGas on a hit, and the stored and returned slices are clones (evm.go lines 53-116). No other precompile is cached. A sync(0x01) gets the same bytes as an uncached call, and balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) parses them the same way.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account use Salvador, which gives five accounts code at block 98,688,600, against other users' funds in the PoolManager?
cleared.result: No. The targets hold no ERC-6909 claims in the six largest currency ids and no PositionManager NFT. A pool that names one of them as hook or currency already fails on every flagged call while the address has no code, and afterwards it reverts. The same holds for a native take to such an address, which only fails the caller's own action (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The sweeper moves only the native balance of its own address.

cleared.check: Does BSC master, the branch that ships Jenner, change opcodes, jump analysis, memory or state relative to v1.8.2? Does Osaka's CLZ, active on BSC since 2026-04-28, meet the bytecode?
cleared.result: 15 core/vm and core/state files are byte-identical between v1.8.2 and master. The develop interpreter differs only by the Pasteur gate on the coinbase rule. A linear disassembly of the 24,009 byte build has no 0x1e (CLZ) opcode outside push data, so the Cancun-targeted bytecode behaves the same under Osaka rules.

cleared.check: Does the libevm pin of avalanchego master (a335c2ecf4df) or uint256 v1.2.4 change an opcode result for the PoolManager?
cleared.result: Of 22 core/vm and core/state files compared between the two libevm commits, only the precompile environment file changes, and it drops the raw caller and self addresses. In uint256 v1.2.4, Mod, MulMod, AddMod and SMod compute into locals and assign z last (uint256.go lines 198-235, 590-760). The AddMod fast path subtracts m at most once, which is enough because x[3] <= m[3] implies x < 2m. The vectors above confirm this on the live node.

cleared.check: Lead L-671: the 10 Avalanche transactions that cycle 12 set aside because no pool key was found, rerun with keys from the Initialize logs of the PoolManager's whole history.
cleared.result: 10 distinct pools, all hookless. Eight have token0 0x1f74f95a... at tick spacing 1 with static fees from 992,682 to 999,882 pips. Two are 1 percent pools at spacing 200. The keys were read through the Routescan log API, and each hashes to its pool id. analyze3.py, rerun from parent-block storage, gives exact for all 10 (removals and claim mints), with 0 storage mismatches.

cleared.check: Lead L-666: the three native-BNB removals of the L-656 window that could not be traced.
cleared.result: Rerun with analyze3.py from parent-block state, using the PoolManager's native balance difference across the block. In 0x1076c3c9 (block 135,480,733, the only PoolManager transaction of its block) the PoolManager paid 15,715,496,722,608,117 wei, which equals what the source owes. In 0x3eab57d7 (block 135,483,276) the block difference equals the 627,249,897,465,861 wei owed, although the block holds other PoolManager transactions. In 0x550fa8b6 the native leg is 0 and the 64,293,145,071,689,188,133 units of token 0x1fa4a73a... equal the Transfer log. Storage after the block matches.

cleared.check: Which validators can run a different code path from the public endpoints?
cleared.result: Polygon: block producers run BlockSTM and the builder. v2.12 adds an opt-in result cache and an opt-in switch dispatch, both read as giving stock results, and the endpoints report three builds (v2.11.1-private, v2.11.1, v2.11.2) with identical core/vm. BSC: validators may run geth from the unpublished commit 4e1c8247 or reth-bsc. Both clients pass every vector, so a disagreement would stop consensus and could not move funds silently. Avalanche: one client and one execution path (saevm). Nothing in these readings changes what the source computes in TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath or TickBitmap.

leads.question: After block 98,688,600, does eth_getCode at the five Salvador addresses equal the sweeper in params/config.go? Does any later bor release add a BlockAlloc entry for an address the PoolManager, PositionManager or a pooled currency or hook uses?
leads.why: BlockAlloc replaces code outside transactions, and it is the one chain mechanism here that could change a pooled token or hook without its owner.

leads.question: Why does bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix) return an empty eth_getLogs result for PoolManager logs in block 135,483,276 when 48.club returns them? Did earlier cycles' BSC log census through that endpoint miss events?
leads.why: Silent gaps in the log source could hide mined transactions from the mined-swap and removal checks.

leadResults.answer: No reachable Polygon endpoint runs bor v2.12.x on 2026-11-24. publicnode reports v2.11.1-private, QuickNode v2.11.1, OnFinality v2.11.2, drpc hides its build, and 1rpc, polygon-rpc.com, Ankr, BlockPi, Nodies and Blast refused or were offline. v2.12.0-beta (2026-11-23) is still a pre-release, and develop carries the same core/vm. The 8,415 memo sequences of cycle 12 stay the baseline to rerun.

github.com/bnb-chain/bsc/commit/4e1c8247 still returns 404, and both dataseed endpoints still report v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104. The public v1.8.2 tag and master, which schedules Jenner for 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC, have byte-identical core/vm and core/state. The unpublished build passes all 185,529 vectors on dataseed1 again this cycle. Which build validators run into Jenner is not public.

v2.12.0 has not shipped. In v2.12.0-beta and develop (identical files), the builder wires the shared caches only into the sealing EVM and the build prefetcher (miner/worker.go lines 1690, 2547-2563, 3072). Each of those runs on its own single-threaded StateDB, and codeReadCache in parallel_statedb.go is byte-identical across v2.11.2, v2.12.0-beta and develop. Recheck when the release ships.

The flag widens the keccak cache, keyed by the whole input as a string, and gives the builder and the serial importer the ecrecover result cache. The ecrecover cache covers only 0x01 with input of at most 128 bytes, keyed by the right-padded 128 byte input, which is ecrecover's own padding. It is bypassed when the precompile set is overridden, charges RequiredGas on a hit, and clones the stored bytes (v2.12.0-beta core/vm/evm.go lines 53-116, ecrecover_cache.go). No other precompile result is cached, so sync(X) on a precompile gets the uncached answer.

Initialize logs for the 10 pool ids, read through the Routescan log API, give keys that hash to the ids. All 10 transactions rerun from parent-block storage match the source to the unit, with 0 storage mismatches (cycles/015/established-l1.work/raw/an3-43114-l671.json).

All three were rerun using the PoolManager's native balance difference across the block. 0x1076c3c9 is alone in its block and paid exactly the 15,715,496,722,608,117 wei owed. 0x3eab57d7's block difference equals the 627,249,897,465,861 wei owed, although the block is shared. 0x550fa8b6 has no native leg, and its token leg matches. Storage after each block matches.
